retention.scope: Regular bytes/raw symlink targets/internal hardlinks retained; sockets/other opaque entries metadata only, not endpoint identity or filesystem losslessness
limits: Sockets and other non-file/directory/symlink entries are retained ONLY as explicit metadata: path, kind, presence, mode, uid/gid, rdev, timestamps and xattrs. No endpoint content, endpoint identity, device contents, or process state is preserved.
This is regular-byte/representable-tree preservation, NOT whole-filesystem losslessness. Inode numbers, atime/ctime, mount identity and external hardlink identities cannot be restored.
Internal regular-file hardlink relationships use tar hardlinks; external hardlink counts are recorded without traversing external paths.
Raw xattrs/ACL metadata and raw path/symlink-target bytes are retained in the inventory manifest. Standard tar extraction alone does not apply custom xattr metadata.

Inactivity evidence is scoped: explicit historical process identities and accessible path-labelled namespace references, with protected-unattributed inspection limits retained. No same-UID ownership inference or host-wide forensic completeness is claimed.
SIGKILL/power loss cannot run cleanup. --recover-only safely removes the registered unique partial and retains published archives and durable failure evidence; it never retries source retirement.
